## Summary

The April 23, 2026 guide starts from the legacy [[source-stripe-inapp-without-card-auth|mobile card integration without bank authentication]]. It modifies the merchant server's PaymentIntent endpoint and the mobile client to handle an issuer's authentication request. The introduction uses `requires_action_not_handled` as diagnosis wording for failures and points to the failed payment in the Dashboard. Treat this as April guide wording. The predecessor's actual example identifies the API error and decline code separately.

The November 7, 2026 capture repeats the migration purpose and supplies navigation for iOS, Android, and React Native. The linked implementation bodies are outside the capture.

## April server changes

1. Remove `error_on_requires_action` so an authentication requirement can produce `requires_action`.
2. Set `confirmation_method: 'manual'` for explicit server reconfirmation after the action.
3. Set `use_stripe_sdk: true` to let the mobile SDK handle authentication.

```javascript
// Abbreviated April example. The original card list has a later API version caveat.
stripe.paymentIntents.create({
    amount: 1099, currency: 'usd',
    confirm: true,
    payment_method: pmId,
    confirmation_method: 'manual',
    use_stripe_sdk: true,
})
```

## Manual confirmation and fulfillment

The client first sends a `payment_method_id`. The server creates and confirms the PaymentIntent. A server-returned `succeeded` on that first attempt can trigger fulfillment immediately. If the Intent is `requires_action`, the example returns `requiresAction: true` and the **PaymentIntent client secret** so the app can launch the SDK authentication modal.

When the required action is successfully handled in this manual flow, the PaymentIntent enters `requires_confirmation`. The client sends the **same PaymentIntent's ID** as `payment_intent_id` and the server calls `paymentIntents.confirm(payment_intent_id)`. Fulfill on server-side `succeeded`. Client action success, cancellation, timeout, and failure describe outcomes at a different boundary. The April guide says the attempt fails back to `requires_payment_method` unless reconfirmed within **one hour**.

The November Confirm API describes a variable upper limit on confirmations, after which another confirm call transitions the Intent to `canceled`. It also says automatic confirmation ordinarily needs no additional confirmation after the SDK handles `next_action`. Manual capture is a distinct setting. With `capture_method: 'manual'`, a successful authorization leads to `requires_capture`.

## April platform examples and later SDK snapshots

### iOS (Objective-C)

The historical example calls `STPPaymentHandler` with an `STPAuthenticationContext` and the Intent client secret. The app sends the Intent ID to the server after `STPPaymentHandlerActionStatusSucceeded`.

```objc
STPPaymentHandler *handler = [STPPaymentHandler sharedHandler];
[handler handleNextActionForPayment:clientSecret
         withAuthenticationContext:self
                         returnURL:nil
                        completion:^(status, paymentIntent, error) {
    // On action success, send the PaymentIntent ID for server reconfirmation.
}];
```

The retained `stripe-ios` **26.11.0** snapshot `2026-09-30-7037819` deprecates that exact selector, `handleNextActionForPayment:withAuthenticationContext:returnURL:completion:`. The wrapper forwards to the newer `handleNextActionForPaymentIntent:authenticationContext:returnURL:completion:` path. See `STPPaymentHandler.swift` lines 398–411 and 2770–2779.

### Android (Java)

The April sample uses `stripe.handleNextActionForPayment(activity, clientSecret)`, followed by `onActivityResult` and `stripe.onPaymentResult(requestCode, data, callback)`. It sends the Intent ID for server reconfirmation when the returned result's action outcome is `SUCCEEDED`.

The retained `stripe-android` **23.25.1** snapshot `2026-10-27-bb0d8d0` keeps `handleNextActionForPayment` and `onPaymentResult`. Its activity overload accepts an AndroidX `ComponentActivity`, and it has a separate `Fragment` overload. The enclosing plain `Activity` in the April example is historical. See `Stripe.kt` lines 280–329 and 344–368.

### React Native

The historical example uses `useStripe().handleCardAction(clientSecret)` and sends `paymentIntent.id` as `payment_intent_id` upon action success. The retained React Native changelog records removal of `handleCardAction` in **0.7.0** in favor of `handleNextAction`. The **0.84.0** snapshot `2026-10-29-33ef1ee` exposes `useStripe().handleNextAction(paymentIntentClientSecret, returnURL?)`. See `CHANGELOG.md` lines 1138–1146, `src/hooks/useStripe.tsx` lines 114–122 and 330–367, and `src/functions.ts` lines 173–201.

## Sandbox test wording

The April variants describe a fake sandbox modal that can simulate successful and failed authentication. In live mode the issuing bank controls the modal content. The April test table nevertheless labels test card `4000002500003155` as failing with decline code `authentication_not_handled` in this integration. This repeats the no-action predecessor's test row. In that predecessor the API example uses `error.code: authentication_required` and `error.decline_code: authentication_not_handled`. The upgrade introduction's `requires_action_not_handled` wording is a separate diagnostic label.

The November Testing guide classifies the same test card as always requiring authentication on-session and requiring it off-session unless set up for future use. See April upgrade lines 184–192, 382–390, and 555–563 and November Testing lines 805–818. The November migration index leaves the April mismatch unresolved. These are documented test cases.

This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:
Instead, the PaymentIntent status changes to `requires_action`.
If successful, the PaymentIntent will have a status of `requires_confirmation` and you need to confirm the PaymentIntent again on your server to finish the payment.
The payment attempt fails and transitions back to `requires_payment_method` if it isn’t confirmed again within one hour.
In live mode the bank controls the UI of what’s displayed inside the modal.
Requires authentication, which in this integration will fail with a decline code of `authentication_not_handled`.

payments-mobile-upgrade-to-handle-action.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/upgrade-to-handle-actions states the goal of migrating a basic mobile card integration to handle issuer authentication and routes iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-15). The April 23, 2026 guide assumes the prior no-action card integration and a merchant server endpoint. A client-supplied PaymentMethod ID starts the payment attempt. The server removes `error_on_requires_action` and creates and confirms the card PaymentIntent with `confirmation_method: 'manual'` and `use_stripe_sdk: true` (old raw lines 12-41). The server's `succeeded` branch can trigger fulfillment immediately. On `requires_action`, the server returns the PaymentIntent client secret so the applicable mobile SDK can prompt authentication. Successful action leaves the PaymentIntent in `requires_confirmation`. The client sends that same PaymentIntent's ID for server reconfirmation and fulfillment follows a final `succeeded` result (old raw lines 72-96, old raw lines 110-126 and old raw lines 139-182). The April guide says the attempt returns to `requires_payment_method` when reconfirmation misses its one-hour window. source-stripe-inapp-upgrade-to-handle-actions.md preserves the flags and ID handoff but skips the intermediate state and the distinction between client action success and payment success. The candidate restores both boundaries and keeps the April timing dated.
payments-mobile-upgrade-to-handle-action.Q2: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/upgrade-to-handle-actions changes the presentation to three links for the same platform variants (new raw lines 9-15). source-stripe-inapp-upgrade-to-handle-actions.md should retain the April 23, 2026 manual path, its one-hour warning, and its dated iOS Objective-C, Android Java and React Native handler examples (old raw lines 91-142, old raw lines 277-340 and old raw lines 473-513). For `@stripe/stripe-react-native` 0.84.0, the retained snapshot `2026-10-29-33ef1ee` exposes `useStripe().handleNextAction`. Its changelog dates removal of the example's `handleCardAction` to 0.7.0 (`CHANGELOG.md:1138-1146`, `src/hooks/useStripe.tsx:114-122,330-367`, `src/functions.ts:173-201`). The `stripe-ios` 26.11.0 snapshot `2026-09-30-7037819` deprecates the historical Objective-C selector while retaining a wrapper that forwards to the newer handler (`STPPaymentHandler.swift:398-411,2770-2779`). The `stripe-android` 23.25.1 snapshot `2026-10-27-bb0d8d0` retains the action and result methods, with `ComponentActivity` for its activity overload (`Stripe.kt:280-329,344-368`). Put these separate package warnings beside the dated platform examples and in the in-app concept's reciprocal route. The old server raw sends `payment_method_types: ["card"]` (old raw lines 32-40 and old raw lines 155-164). The separately captured `2026-09-30.endive` changelog's endpoint links and REST table document PaymentIntent create rejecting that request field with HTTP 400 and `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported`. The response field remains readable. Dynamic payment methods and the allowed or excluded request controls are distinct alternatives. Link that version boundary by the old raw and preserve its confirmation-mode and SDK-handling flags as dated workflow evidence (`raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:5-24,28,34-36`). An SDK action callback signals action handling. Server-confirmed `succeeded` is the fulfillment boundary in the guide. The November Confirm API separately distinguishes automatic mode, manual capture, and a variable limit on repeated manual confirmation (`raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-confirm-2026-11-07.md:7-17`). In April, the sandbox modal can simulate authentication success or failure and the live issuer controls modal content. The repeated row still says the authentication-required test card fails with `authentication_not_handled` (old raw lines 184-192 and old raw lines 555-563). The April no-action predecessor shows that value as a decline code with API error `authentication_required`, while the April upgrade intro uses `requires_action_not_handled` (old raw lines 12-17; `raw/stripe-inapp-without-card-auth-2025.md:290-325`). The November testing page describes the same test card's on-session authentication requirement (`raw/stripe-testing-2026-11-07.md:805-818`). Preserve the diagnostic and test-table mismatch on both guide routes with date and field scope. The November index supplies variant navigation. The separate packages and changelog establish version-specific interfaces, and the evidence stops short of a tested migration or payment. The candidate records these version warnings and the sandbox mismatch.
